findings.explanation: The job invokes an HTTPS target (typically Cloud Run) but did not expose attempt_deadline. GCP defaults this to 3 minutes; a cold-starting Cloud Run service or a slow downstream call can exceed that, causing the job to be marked failed even though the target would have succeeded given more time.
findings.remediation: Added variable "attempt_deadline" (default "180s", matching the existing GCP default so behavior is unchanged) and wired it into the resource, so consumers can raise it for slower targets.
findings.title: Cloud Scheduler job has no configurable attempt_deadline

findings.explanation: google_cloud_scheduler_job supports a description argument shown in the GCP console. Without it, operators have to cross-reference Terraform source to know why a given job exists.
findings.remediation: Added optional variable "description" (default null) and wired it into the resource.
findings.title: Cloud Scheduler job has no description

suggested_policies.rationale: Cloud Scheduler jobs invoking HTTP targets (frequently Cloud Run, which can cold-start) rely on the GCP default attempt_deadline of 3 minutes unless it's explicitly set. Flagging its absence surfaces a class of jobs that will silently fail on slow-starting targets.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_XXX  # run: holden next-id --cloud GCP
name: Cloud Scheduler jobs should set an explicit attempt_deadline
principle: reliability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  Without an explicit attempt_deadline, GCP applies a 3-minute default. HTTP
  targets that cold-start (e.g. Cloud Run scaled to zero) or have variable
  latency can exceed this, causing the scheduled run to be marked failed even
  though the target would have completed given more time.
remediation: |
  Set attempt_deadline explicitly, sized to the target's expected worst-case
  latency:
    resource "google_cloud_scheduler_job" "example" {
      attempt_deadline = "300s"
    }
resources:
  google_cloud_scheduler_job:
    path: attempt_deadline
    not_null: true

suggested_policies.rationale: A description on the job is cheap to add and makes the job's purpose visible in the GCP console without needing to cross-reference source. Concrete, single-attribute, unambiguous.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_XXX  # run: holden next-id --cloud GCP
name: Cloud Scheduler jobs should have a description
principle: maintainability
severity: INFO
rationale: |
  Undocumented scheduler jobs are hard to identify in the GCP console,
  especially in projects with many jobs across teams.
remediation: |
  Add a description:
    resource "google_cloud_scheduler_job" "example" {
      description = "Nightly reconciliation of order totals"
    }
resources:
  google_cloud_scheduler_job:
    path: description
    not_null: true
